InitialDescription: Rice is mild and clean. It needs steady grinding, but too much force can make it taste burnt.
Tea leaves taste bitter at first and sweet later. Slow grinding helps the sweetness come out.
Black sesame has a strong roasted flavor. It can lead a recipe, but too much makes it bitter.
Glutinous rice makes the mixture smooth and thick. It should support stronger flavors.
Peanut gives a warm roasted flavor. It works well with other nutty ingredients.
Red bean is thick and gently sweet. It works well as a base flavor.
Dried tangerine peel is bright and slightly bitter. It works best as a small accent.
Rock sugar adds clean sweetness. It should round out the recipe instead of taking over.
Sand ginger is deep and spicy. It needs enough force to bring out its flavor.
Coarse salt supports other flavors. Use it lightly so it does not become the main taste.
White pepper is sharp and quick to spread. Too much grinding can make it harsh.
Lotus leaf is light and fresh. It can be covered easily by stronger ingredients.
Yangjiang douchi is savory and fermented. It gives the recipe a strong base.
Ginger is fresh and sharp. It can brighten a recipe, but it can also become too strong.
Scallion white is fresh and light. It works best near the end of a recipe.
